Dharampal Premchand Ltd., Through its General Manager (Legal & Commercial) Shashi Kumar Maheshwari, A-34 & 35, Sector 60, Noida-201301, Utter Pradesh and Anr. ....Petitioners. Versus The State of Maharashtra and Ors. ....Respondents. Mr. Brijesh Kumar h/f. Mr. N.S. Tekale, Advocate for petitioners. Mr. S.G. Sangle, App for respondents. Coram : T.V. Nalawade And Shrikant D. Kulkarni, Jj. Dated : 03/11/2020.
texts.facts: 1. The petition is fled to challenge the order dated 20.7.2018 issued by Commissioner under Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 to prohibit transportation of Gutkha and similar items under section 30(2)(a) of this Special Enactment. It is contended that the order issued is illegal and void as the Commissioner has no power to impose ban on transportation. The petitioner is manufacturer of articles including chewing tobacco and it has manufacturing unit at Noida, Utter Pradesh. Both the sides are heard. 2. The petition is fled by manufacturing company through its General Manager and petitioner No. 2 appears to be a person who is in control of the things of the company. It is their contention that on 18.12.2018 the consignment of product, of chewing product was being transported from Noida to purchaser from Bidar, Karnataka in a truck. It is contended that on 22.12.2018 the truck was intercepted in Maharashtra, in Degloor Tahsil and the truck was taken by police to police station. It is contended that on 24.12.2018 Food Safety Officer checked the contents of the truck and gave complaint to police that the transportation was in violation of prohibitory order issued under Food Safety and Standards Act and then crime came to be registered. The contents of the truck came to be M/S Dharampal Premchand Ltd. It appears that in the past Criminal Application No. 250/2019 was fled in respect of the said action of the police and Food Safety Officer, but this Court dismissed the criminal application which was fled for quashing of the crime. It appears that the truck was released by the learned J.M.F.C., but the goods were not released. Even when the decision given by this Court in Criminal Application No. 250/2019 was challenged by fling Special Leave Petition (Criminal) Diary No(s).31844/2019 in Supreme Court and the said proceeding came to be dismissed, the present proceeding is fled. 4. It can be said that the previous proceeding, Criminal Application No. 250/2019 was fled for the company as the company would have been beneftted if the F.I.R. was [LEAKAGE_MASK] by this Court. It was submitted that the company is not made accused though company ought to have made accused in such a case. It is clear that the persons who were controlling the company were behind Criminal Application No. 250/2019 and now by taking the name of the company, they have fled the present proceeding. Thus, the petitioners intend to reopen the matter which is decided by this Court on merits in the past. 5. The contentions made in the previous proceeding are quoted by this Court at para No. 4 and they are as under :-
texts.arguments: " 4) The learned counsel for the applicant, driver of the truck, submitted that tobacco was being transported from Uttar Pradesh to Bidar, Karnataka. He has produced tax invoices in respect of some of the materials which are shown to be seized. He submitted that under the notifcation in question of the Commissioner of Food and Drugs Administration, Maharashtra State, though there is ban on manufacture, storage, distribution, transportation or sale of tobacco which is either favoured, sainted or mixed with any of the said adhesives under the provisions of section 30 (2) (a) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act") there could not have been prohibition on transportation. He also submitted that in view of provisions of Articles 19, 301 and 304 of the Constitution of India, such prohibition order also could not have been issued. Admittedly, these articles are banned in Maharashtra under the aforesaid notifcation for the aforesaid purposes. The said notifcation is not challenged in the present proceeding and relief of only quashing of the F.I.R. is claimed." Which substances are covered under Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 is considered and law in that regard is laid down in the case reported as 2013 (2) Bom.C.R. 383 [Dhariwal Industries Limited and Anr. Vs. State of Maharashtra and Ors.]. This Court considered the provision of Article 19 of Constitution of India in this reported case and also in the case of Vishnu Pouch Packaging Pvt. Ltd. cited supra. 7) The decision of Criminal Application No. 250/2019 was challenged in Supreme Court by Naushad s/o. Babu Khan and Anr., the person who probably controls the company.
